text:
miguel.sec: Heads-up: org-wide security advisory — service principal (app) credential lifecycle enforcement. Starting 2026-05-01 we will automatically disable app secrets older than 90 days and remove orphaned service principals. This is to reduce risk from long-lived secrets and align with our short-lived-credential policy. https://redwood.internal/runbooks/sp-lifecycle :rotating_light:

deploy-bot: weekly-sp-scan report attached. Found 142 SPs with secrets >90 days, 37 orphaned SPs, 12 SPs with excessive IAM roles (admin-ish). Top offenders by service tag: payments, telemetry, migration-worker. Report: https://redwood.internal/reports/sp-scan-2090012345

sarah.ops: timeline? will this affect Dedicated/private clusters?

miguel.sec: enforcement window: 2026-05-01 auto-disable. We will send owner DMs starting 2026-04-10 and a second reminder 2026-04-20. Private deployments: control plane will emit notices but we cannot auto-disable remote on-prem secrets; customers must follow the runbook.

ryan.eng: can we get an export of SPs owned by our payments team (team=payments tag)?

deploy-bot: @ryan.eng requested list generated. Command: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_TOKEN" https://api.redwood.internal/infra/service-principals?tag=team:payments` — output will be DM'ed in 15m.

miguel.sec: Action items for owners (short):
1) rotate any app secrets/keys older than 90 days OR migrate to OIDC/GitHub Actions OIDC roles.
2) remove unused SPs and add owner metadata (team, owner-email).
3) reduce scopes to least-privilege; use per-route roles rather than org-admin.
4) open a ticket if you need an exception (5 business day SLA to review).

kate-platform: this will break a few CI jobs unless we rotate. Suggest we bulk-migrate CI to OIDC next week. Is there a migration helper?

miguel.sec: yes, we have a helper script and a sample GitHub Actions trust policy in the runbook. Minimal example for GitHub Actions -> AWS OIDC role trust (example):
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [{
    "Effect": "Allow",
    "Principal": {"Federated": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:oidc-provider/token.actions.githubusercontent.com"},
    "Action": "sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity",
    "Condition": {"StringLike": {"token.actions.githubusercontent.com:sub": "repo:yourorg/yourrepo:*"}}
  }]
}
```

miguel.sec: For Azure app secrets, rotate with: `az ad app credential reset --id <APP_ID> --credential-description "rotated-2026-04"`
For GCP SA keys: `gcloud iam service-accounts keys create key.json --iam-account=<SA_EMAIL>` then delete old keys with `gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete <KEY_ID>`
For AWS IAM user access keys: `aws iam create-access-key --user-name <user>` then `aws iam delete-access-key --access-key-id <old>`

olivia-sre: will the auto-disable produce a 403 on production endpoints? We need a grace period for critical routes.

miguel.sec: auto-disable will block token issuance tied to the disabled secret; for infra critical routes we recommend adding a secondary short-lived credential or OIDC role. If you expect outages, file an exception request (label: sp-exception). Exceptions are temporary and require mitigation plan.

ryan.eng: thanks — will start inventorying and open tickets for three legacy services.

sarah.ops: can security provide a CSV with owner emails so we can create tickets at scale?

deploy-bot: CSV export queued; will DM owners for top-100 highest-risk SPs and post full CSV to the runbook page for org admins.

miguel.sec: Summary/action checklist (short):
- Owners: rotate/migrate or add owner metadata by 2026-04-20.
- Security: will run final enforcement scan 2026-04-25 and auto-disable 2026-05-01.
- If you need help, contact sec-automations@redwood.com or open ticket in #help.

kate-platform: ack, will schedule a migration sprint.

olivia-sre: noted, adding monitoring runbook to critical alerts to detect 403 regressions.

miguel.sec: appreciate it. We'll post weekly progress updates in this channel. If you want your team's list sooner ping me or DM deploy-bot. :white_check_mark:
